summary.headline: Devson H1 FY27 revenue rose just 1.14% to INR31.69 crore, but EBITDA margin expanded 250 bps to 31.80% as catalysts offset weak exports.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR31.69 crore in H1 FY27, up 1.14% YoY, while EBITDA grew 9.84% to INR10.25 crore and PAT rose 13.12% to INR7.5 crore. Export share fell to 6.72% from 42.95% because Strait of Hormuz disruption hit Middle East shipments, and domestic sales carried the half. Catalyst sales rose to INR25.31 crore from INR13.26 crore, while ceramic ball sales fell to INR3.81 crore from INR13.45 crore. The company listed on BSE SME in July 2026 raising INR39.39 crore, and a 5,088 MTPA capacity addition is targeted for Q1 FY28.

segments.name: Catalyst
segments.commentary: Revenue INR25.31 crore in H1 FY27 vs INR13.26 crore in H1 FY26, roughly double; management calls it the higher-value, higher-margin product.

segments.name: Ceramic balls
segments.commentary: Revenue INR3.81 crore vs INR13.45 crore a year earlier, down sharply as Middle East ceramic ball business was hit by Hormuz disruption.

segments.name: Adsorbent
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2.49 crore vs INR4.28 crore in H1 FY26, declining.

guidance_outlook: New 5,088 MTPA facility (total installed capacity to 11,293 MTPA from 6,205 MTPA, about 82% expansion) expected operational in Q1 FY28.
Management targets about 50% utilisation of the new facility by the end of FY28, with up to 80% utilisation referenced for the new plant.
Management expects H2 revenue to rise sharply if Hormuz shipping normalises; no formal FY28 growth guidance was given beyond maintaining past growth.
Majority of current one-time orders expected to be completed in FY27; contractual orders (about 100 tonnes) are call-off based with no firm timing.
Third facility planned after second facility reaches about 70-80% utilisation; land already acquired.
capex_capacity: Existing Wadhwan, Gujarat installed capacity of 6,205 MTPA; planned addition of 5,088 MTPA to reach 11,293 MTPA.
New facility: about 5,000 MT capacity on about 4,000 sq m area, versus about 7,000 sq m for the existing plant; new plant to be more automated.
Construction: PEB structures ordered, labour orders complete; civil erection about 3 months after Diwali; machinery to be ordered within 15 days and installed in 3-4 months.
IPO proceeds used for the new manufacturing facility; INR12 crore allocated to long-term working capital, of which INR4.14 crore used by Sep 30, 2026.
Capacity is fungible between catalyst and adsorbent products, per management.
demand_pricing: Export share fell to 6.72% of H1 FY27 revenue from 42.95% in H1 FY26; domestic share 93.28%. Export business was about 70-80% Middle East in FY26.
Export order book stated at about INR25-28 crore, similar to last year; export vs domestic split not disclosed on call.
Sea freight for a 20-ft container reportedly rose from about USD 600-800 to about USD 6,000-8,000 (about 10x), constraining exports.
Raw materials about 97% indigenous per management; natural gas cost doubled but was passed through to customers.
Competitor cited: Sud-Chemie Clariant (German MNC with an Indian plant, unlisted). Entry barriers cited as proven-performance and refinery-experience tender requirements.
Appointed a business development head from an MNC to target Russia, Africa and South Korea; US business hit by tariffs.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split across catalyst, adsorbent and ceramic balls for H1; current order book and tender pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Catalyst grew faster than ceramic balls. Segment values: ceramic INR3.81 crore vs INR13.45 crore; adsorbent INR2.49 crore vs INR4.28 crore; catalyst INR25.31 crore vs INR13.26 crore. Export order book about INR25-28 crore; tender pipeline value to be shared later.

qa_highlights.question: Expected commissioning and utilisation of the new 5,000 MT capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Operational in Q1 FY28, with about 50% utilisation targeted by end of FY28; the plant could reach saturation earlier if new products are commercialised.

qa_highlights.question: Will the outstanding H2-shifted orders be completed in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: One-time orders should complete in FY27; contractual call-off orders (about 100 tonnes) have no firm timing.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue potential of the two plants at 80% utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR100 crore was possible at 80% but depends on product mix; higher-margin products could take it beyond that.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to Middle East and what is the diversification plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Middle East was about 70-80% of export business in FY26; diversification into Russia, Africa, South Korea and US, with a new BD head appointed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower exports reduced freight costs proportionately, which lowered other expenses.

risks_watch: Hormuz disruption: export recovery and H2 revenue step-up depend on shipping normalising; freight costs have risen roughly 10x.
Execution risk on new facility timeline (Q1 FY28) and ramp to 50% utilisation.
Customer concentration: export business heavily reliant on Middle East.
Order visibility is weak: export book about INR25-28 crore, with no split or tender pipeline quantified; contractual orders timing uncertain.
PE catalyst project: cage and physical trials complete, chemical results pending.
Revenue growth only 1.14% despite strong margin expansion; monitor whether catalyst momentum continues as ceramic balls decline.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins, catalyst growth and capacity plans, but evasive on order book details, tender pipeline, realisations and Hormuz outlook, deferring several answers to follow-up calls. Management repeatedly tied H2 upside to Hormuz normalisation.
key_quotes: So, all the orders we have on hand, majorly of our one-time orders, so that will be going to be completed by this financial year.
As I told in my answer like catalyst businesses increased, but because of Hormuz we were doing many businesses of ceramic ball in Middle East.
Right now, export books might be same as last year, around INR25 crores to INR28 crores, that much.

adds.what: 5,088 MTPA new Wadhwan, Gujarat facility (total installed to 11,293 MTPA from 6,205 MTPA)

growth.why: No formal FY28 revenue guidance; H1 FY27 revenue up only 1.14% with exports collapsing to 6.72% share on Hormuz disruption, while a 5,088 MTPA plant targeted for Q1 FY28 (about 1 quarter out) is backed by PEB orders and civil work timelines but 50% utilisation only by end FY28 and no firm call-off timing.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 250 bps to 31.80% in H1 FY27 on catalyst mix (catalyst revenue INR25.31 crore vs INR13.26 crore) and freight-driven lower other expenses, though Hormuz-linked export weakness caps upside.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 5,088 MTPA Wadhwan facility (installed capacity 6,205 to 11,293 MTPA, about 82% increase) is under construction with PEB structures ordered and management guiding operational in Q1 FY28, though 50% utilisation only by end FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 revenue rose only 1.14% to INR31.69 crore with exports down to 6.72% of revenue from 42.95%, so volume recovery depends on Hormuz shipping normalising and export book of INR25-28 crore converting.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 83% and the new 5,088 MTPA plant is already being built, while a third facility is planned once the second reaches 70-80% utilisation on land already acquired.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects H2 revenue to rise sharply only if Hormuz shipping normalises, and no formal FY28 growth guidance was given, so an upgrade is conditional.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revenue grew just 1.14% in H1 FY27, export order book is about INR25-28 crore with no split or tender pipeline quantified, and freight costs rose about 10x (USD 600-800 to USD 6,000-8,000 per 20-ft container).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management said the new plant could saturate earlier if new products are commercialised, and the PE catalyst project has cage and physical trials complete with chemical results pending, but no launch date was given.

rows.label: Export diversification to Russia, Africa, South Korea
rows.why: A new business development head from an MNC was appointed to target Russia, Africa and South Korea, but Middle East was about 70-80% of FY26 exports and no revenue figures were given for these markets.

rows.label: Export order book INR25-28 crore
rows.why: The export order book is about INR25-28 crore, similar to last year, but its split and the tender pipeline were not quantified and contractual call-off orders (about 100 tonnes) have no firm timing.

rows.label: Hormuz normalisation driving export and ceramic ball recovery
rows.why: Exports fell to 6.72% of revenue from 42.95% and ceramic ball sales fell to INR3.81 crore from INR13.45 crore, so recovery hinges on shipping normalising, which management did not forecast.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins, catalyst growth and the Q1 FY28 capacity plan, but evasive on order book split, tender pipeline, realisations and the Hormuz outlook, deferring several answers; analysts pushed on order visibility and Middle East dependence.
